title: What tech should i use ??
author: Resurrec_Barbar
selftext:
Our lives are limited and i have never created anything (aside from job and projects ) . I have had this idea but i never had the time to execute it on a large scale as i dont know gamedev

  
I want to create a RPG based on my favourite novel . I want to bring the world to life .A world of my own

  
Its plain 2D like classic snes ones and Stardew valley . What is the best game engine + agent to do it as quick as possible and how much it gonna cost me ??

comments.author: United-Tour5043
comments.body:
you need to search for the tech stack that most game engines use, or use a game engine trough an MCP.

plan thoroughly every nook and crany, and atomize HEAVILY each step. you need the most abslute solid base to start even considering building the game.

you are basically creating a software from scratch, learn how games initiate development, and mimic all that.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body:
Most of your effort needs to be in game design.  You need to understand what makes a game a game, what makes a game good, how to achieve the feeling you want in the player, game flow, juice, etc.  

It would also be good to understand the architecture of games, how systems are built.  Some top level CS or coding understanding would be good.  It'll give you a good idea what what can be achieved (you dont need to know how anymore), what what options you have to achieve your goal.  ((Or prompt the AI to give you all the options and a breakdown of their strengths and weaknesses))

AI can use Unity and Unreal, but a coding first engine is faster.  AI doesn't really understand 3d space or visuals, but it's really really good at code.  

I haven't found a good workflow for making animations.  I have ok workflows for making 2d or 3d assets.  Still a lot of work our the human side through.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
like, even with AI, some big RPG is kinda hard

pick a tool and figure out what you can make

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: It took me 2 weeks working heavily with AI to just design the skill progression system for my arpg.    The design is the hard part.  Once you have the design (in a design document) that becomes your prompt and the AI can make it.  Then you need to test it, attack it, and figure out all the parts where your design was weak or vague.
